ops.title: Never git-checkout/revert unexplained working-tree changes — they are often the user's own mid-session edits (e.g. the actions/checkout@v7 bumps I wrongly reverted twice); surface them instead.
ops.body:
Do not revert uncommitted working-tree changes you didn't make, even when they look like out-of-scope agent contamination. In fusekit I twice ran `git checkout --` on `actions/checkout@v6→v7` bumps in `.github/workflows/`, assuming an agent had slipped them in — they were the user's own edits, and he had to tell me to "stop reverting that, put back all the updated actions."

**Why:** the user edits and commits in these repos mid-session (see [[reverify-commits-before-extracting]]). An unexplained diff is more likely his work than contamination, and reverting destroys it silently.

**How to apply:** when the tree has changes I can't account for, leave them in place and mention them to the user (or commit them separately if they'd otherwise be swept into an unrelated commit). Only revert changes I watched an agent make, verified against that agent's actual file set.
